interest: Shows U.S. tracking of 1938 Japanese civil law revisions and reciprocal judicial aid for foreign courts.
overview: This file from the U.S. State Department's decimal file 894.0442 covers civil laws, statutes, and judicial procedures of Japan between October 1935 and August 1938. The records consist of a 1935 congressional inquiry by Representative W. G. Andrews and Secretary of State Cordell Hull's reply providing the text of Article 175 of the Japanese Code of Civil Procedure regarding international service of process; official despatches from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo transmitting complete English translations of Law No. 19 of 1938 (revising the Code of Civil Procedure) and Law No. 18 of 1938 (revising the Civil Code); interdepartmental correspondence with the Department of Justice acknowledging receipt of the procedural revisions; and an internal State Department memorandum analyzing amendments to Japan's Law for Reciprocal Aid in Compliance with the Requests of Foreign Courts.
